newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI lifts credit curbs on major commodities.
newsitem.headline: India RBI lifts credit curbs on major commodities.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday said it exempted oilseeds, oils, sugar and cotton from selective credit controls following an improved supply of these commodities.

"In the context of the favourable supply situation, all the above mentioned commodities, except buffer stock and the unreleased stocks of sugar to sugar mills, are exempted from all stipulations of selective credit controls effective October 21," the RBI said.
"Banks are free to fix prudential margins on advances against sensitive commodities," the RBI said in its credit policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
The RBI said the minimum margin on unreleased stocks of sugar is being lowered by 5.0 percentage points from the existing 20 percent to 15 percent effective October 21, 1996.
"In the case of buffer stock sugar, the existing prescription of a zero percent will continue," it said.
Presently bank advances against pulses, coarse foodgrains, oilseeds and oils, sugar and cotton are subject to selective credit controls.
Traders have been complaining of low trading volumes in commodities because of the credit sqeeze.
